clue.text: Sailors on tub needed to soften water

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for the noun: what is needed to soften water

indicators.note: in an across clue one thing on another sits after it, so the first-named piece goes second

parts.note: a bath is a tub for washing in
old salts are seasoned sailors

explanation.surface: A crew of sailors is sitting on a tub to make the water softer.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'Sailors on tub' puts the sailors after the tub.
explanation.definitionFit: Bath salts are crystals dissolved in a bath, traditionally used to make hard water gentler on skin.

clue.text: Old community found in outskirts of British wood

indicators.note: found in places the first group inside the edge letters
the outskirts of a word are its edge letters, first and last

parts.note: the first and last letters of British
the European Economic Community, the former name of the EU

explanation.surface: An old settlement is discovered on the edge of a British forest.
explanation.definitionFit: Beech is the timber of the beech tree, a common hardwood, so it names a type of wood.

clue.text: Tease performing in Somerset town

parts.note: to taunt is to tease
a performer who is on is on stage

explanation.surface: Someone teases a performer in a West Country town.
explanation.walkthrough: Somerset is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Taunton is the county town of Somerset, a county in south-west England.

clue.text: Don't go out without your cap? It's a shame

indicators.note: the cap of a word is its first letter, and without says it is removed

parts.note: the opposite of going out is to stay in
the first letter of your

explanation.surface: A warning to wear a hat outdoors, or else it would be a pity.
explanation.walkthrough: Y is removed from STAY IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A stain on one's name is a mark of disgrace, so it is a source of shame or dishonour.

clue.text: South Americans occupying flat in Osaka

indicators.note: occupying means sitting within, so the letters lie inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: Some South Americans are living in an apartment in Japan.
explanation.definitionFit: Latinos are people of Latin American origin, which includes those from South American countries.

clue.text: Flash poseur dancing around her, for example

indicators.note: around says the rearranged letters wrap the next word
dancing letters move about and settle in a different order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: A showy poser dances around a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flash' looks like an adjective for showy, matching poseur, but it is the DC comics character. 'For example' marks the definition as an instance.
explanation.definitionFit: The Flash is a DC Comics character with super speed, one example of a costumed crime-fighter.

clue.text: Dues to be paid for players not starting

definitions.meaning: first meaning: membership fees, short for subscriptions
second meaning: substitutes waiting on the bench

explanation.surface: A club's fees must be paid even for the players left on the bench.
explanation.definitionFit: The short plural form covers both subscription payments to a club and substitute players kept in reserve.

clue.text: Transmit clue hidden inside for a small fee

indicators.note: something hidden inside is tucked within, so the second word goes into the first

parts.note: to send is to transmit
a tip is a hint or clue

explanation.surface: Sending a hint secretly in exchange for a modest payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hidden inside' tempts a search for a hidden word, but here it puts one synonym inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: A stipend is a fixed allowance or modest salary, such as one paid to a student or a cleric.

clue.text: Crown reportedly understands the outcome of excess flattery

indicators.note: reportedly means as told, so the words are judged by their spoken sound

parts.note: the crown of a hill is its brow, the top
to understand is to know

explanation.surface: The monarchy is said to grasp what too much fawning leads to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brow knows' said quickly runs together into the answer. The definition is a joke: a sycophant's nose ends up soiled from kissing up.
explanation.definitionFit: Brown-nosing is grovelling sycophancy; the crude image is a nose dirtied by kissing a superior's backside.

clue.text: One for the first time playing tuba in pit

indicators.note: in places the reworked letters inside the word that follows

parts.note: a pit is a small hollow or dent in a surface

indicators.note: playing an instrument suggests its letters can be performed in a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A newcomer plays the tuba in the orchestra pit for the very first time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pit' suggests the orchestra pit, but here it is a hollow in a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A debutant is someone making a first appearance, a novice doing something publicly for the first time.

clue.text: Fancy an idea containing this, for example

definitions.text: Fancy an idea containing this, for example

parts.note: surface reading: an offer, would you like a notion with this in it?
setter's reading: a fancy or idea can carry something harmful, as in a mind corrupted by a toxic notion

explanation.surface: Someone offers you an idea with something in it, like a waiter offering a dish.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Fancy' as a noun meaning an idea; a fancy that contains something toxic is a corrupting thought, and the answer is the toxic thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Poison is any substance that harms when taken in, and figuratively a corrupting influence that can taint thoughts.

clue.text: Name on picture provides some illumination

parts.note: a photo is a picture
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: Writing a name on a photograph helps shed light on who is shown.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'Name on picture' puts N after PHOTO.
explanation.definitionFit: A photon is a single quantum of light, so it is a tiny portion of the light around us.

clue.text: Neck point involved in transmission of feeling

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for the noun: something involved in transmitting feeling

parts.note: neck as in cheek or audacity, which is nerve
the point of something is its end

explanation.surface: A point on the neck plays a part in passing on sensation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neck' looks anatomical, fitting the surface, but it means brazen cheek.
explanation.definitionFit: A nerve ending is the terminal part of a nerve fibre that picks up touch, heat or pain signals.

clue.text: Switches new ingredient for drinks

indicators.note: an ingredient goes into a mixture, so the letter is put inside the word that follows

parts.note: swigs are large gulps of drink
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Someone changes to a new ingredient for their cocktails.
explanation.walkthrough: N goes inside SWIGS between the I and the G.
explanation.definitionFit: To swing is to change direction or allegiance, so swings and switches both describe shifting suddenly.

clue.text: Great flow under ground

indicators.note: ground means crushed, as in a mill, so the letters are broken up and remade

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A great river runs underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' looks like a noun, the earth the water flows beneath, but it is the past participle of grind.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are enthusiastic adjectives of approval meaning excellent, marvellous or extremely good.

clue.text: Family time in spot that's fittingly close

indicators.note: in places the first two pieces inside the word that follows

parts.note: to spot something is to sight it
kin are one's family
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Relatives spending time in one place are pleasantly snug together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spot' is a verb here, to catch sight of, not a place.
explanation.definitionFit: Skintight clothing fits the body very tightly, pressing as close to it as skin, so it is snug in fit.

clue.text: Be reasonable, when regular partner is working

parts.note: a steady is someone you are going out with regularly
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A plea for calm about a boyfriend or girlfriend who has a job.
explanation.definitionFit: The interjection urges someone to calm down and not get carried away, the same as asking them to be sensible.

clue.text: Slating's broken in new house? Put it on this

definitions.text: in new house? Put it on this

indicators.note: something broken has its parts scattered, so the letters come apart and regroup

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A buyer finds broken roof slates in a new house and wants them noted.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'S of 'Slating's' supplies the eighth letter. A snag list records defects a builder must fix in a newly built home.
explanation.definitionFit: Buyers of a newly built home compile a list of faults for the builder, so a broken slate goes on it.

clue.text: Seriousness will tend to keep you grounded

definitions.meaning: first meaning: solemnity, weightiness of manner

definitions.text: will tend to keep you grounded
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the physical force pulling bodies towards the earth

explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads as advice that a serious nature keeps you level-headed; literally it describes the force that stops you floating off.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means solemn dignity of manner and also the force of attraction holding objects on the earth's surface.

clue.text: Decent amount to clear up problem?

parts.note: to tidy is to clear up
a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: A question of whether a fair amount will resolve a difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: A tidy sum is an informal expression for a considerable sum of money, a substantial quantity.

clue.text: Both sides abandon long aspect when gambling

indicators.note: the two sides, first and last letters, leave each of the following words

parts.note: taken as written, before its outer letters go
taken as written, before its outer letters go

explanation.surface: Someone drops a long-held view of things once they start betting.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something on spec means acting speculatively, taking a chance without a guarantee of return.

clue.text: Being virtuous is not commonly involved in being devious

indicators.note: something involved in a thing is wrapped up within it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: sly means cunning or devious
ain't is the colloquial, non-standard form of is not

explanation.surface: Goodness has nothing to do with being cunning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commonly' flags informal, non-standard speech, so the contraction used by many speakers is wanted rather than the standard phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Saintly describes a person of great holiness and goodness, behaving like a saint, morally upright.

clue.text: Socialist pretended to be held back before publication

parts.note: red is the traditional colour and nickname for a socialist
to act is to pretend

explanation.surface: A left-wing figure faked being restrained before a book came out.
explanation.definitionFit: Redacted text has been censored or blacked out, withheld from a document before it is released.

clue.text: Grooming hard worker to take time for run

indicators.note: taking one thing for another means swapping: a time letter comes in where a run letter stood

parts.note: a toiler works hard
T is the abbreviation for time
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A hard-working employee pauses to tidy up before going out for a jog.
explanation.walkthrough: The final R of TOILER is replaced by T.
explanation.definitionFit: Toilet in its older sense is the process of washing, dressing and arranging one's hair, as in toilet water.

clue.text: Part of support that Iran bought in America originally

indicators.note: originally points to the origin of each word, its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letters of these five words

explanation.surface: Iran buys military backing from the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Support' looks political or military, but it is the leg holding up the body.
explanation.definitionFit: The tibia is the shinbone, one of the main bones of the leg that holds up the body's weight.

clue.text: Part of mirror reflection shows up fault

indicators.note: in a down entry going up means the letters are read from the bottom
part of says only a stretch of the following letters is used

parts.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.surface: Looking closely at a reflection reveals a flaw in the glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reflection' suits the theme of reversal, but the indicator is 'shows up', apt in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An error is a mistake or flaw, so it is a synonym of fault in the sense of a blunder.

clue.text: Sound hesitant leaving presentation for execution in America

indicators.note: something leaving departs, so those letters drop out of the word that follows

parts.note: an offering is something presented
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A nervous speaker walks out of a talk about capital punishment in the US.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is removed from OFFERING. To off someone is American slang for to kill them.
explanation.definitionFit: In US slang to off someone is to kill them, so the noun form is a killing or execution.

clue.text: Boss upset by right-wing whinging

definitions.note: a whinging tale: the answer is a noun

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters fall into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A manager is annoyed by a right-wing colleague's constant complaining.
explanation.definitionFit: A sob story is a tale of woe told to win sympathy, which is exactly what whining amounts to.

clue.text: Friend declared a position

indicators.note: declared means spoken out, so what counts is how the words are pronounced

parts.note: the lie of something is its position, as in the lie of the land

explanation.surface: A friend announced where they stood.
explanation.definitionFit: An ally is someone on your side who supports you, a companion or partner in a cause.

clue.text: Twain boy most upset by solicitor dropping line

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters fall into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

indicators.note: dropping something lets it fall away, so one letter is lost

parts.note: a solicitor is a kind of lawyer
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: Mark Twain's young hero is badly shaken by a lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a solicitor is a type of lawyer who handles legal work outside court.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom Sawyer is the boy hero of Mark Twain's 1876 novel about life on the Mississippi.
